subject.title: [Security] Plaintext credential leakage in diagnostic crash dumps

question: Does a disclosure-safe canary survive `openclaw gateway diagnostics export` on current main or the latest release, requiring private advisory handling and a redaction fix?
rationale: The public report alleges credential exposure but provides no exact canary, exported artifact, tested SHA, or demonstrated current boundary crossing; maintainers must validate it without encouraging public secret disclosure.

options.title: Request private canary proof
options.body: Ask the reporter to provide a synthetic credential payload, exact generation steps, affected version or SHA, and sanitized bundle structure through the private security channel.

options.title: Confirm and repair privately
options.body: If maintainers reproduce the leak, patch the dedicated diagnostic support-redaction path and add current-release and current-main export regression tests before disclosure.

options.title: Close after failed validation
options.body: If exact canary testing on current main and the claimed release does not reproduce, close with the tested encodings and versions documented.

recommendation.title: Request private canary proof
recommendation.body: Ask the reporter to provide a synthetic credential payload, exact generation steps, affected version or SHA, and sanitized bundle structure through the private security channel.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and hardened the diagnostics export and redaction modules that own the alleged behavior.
